title: Corporate Travel Programmes: What an Amendment May and May Not Change
content:
An amendment changes the contracted particulars of a programme under the Corporate Travel Programmes: the contracted seats, the invoicing arrangement or the administrator's details. These are the limits on what it may reach.

**Seats.** The contracted seat count may be changed within the tier's seat range, and a change outside that range is a tier change rather than an amendment.

**Invoicing frequency.** The invoicing frequency may be changed only at a period boundary, and a change from annual to monthly does not entitle the company to a refund of the annual subscription already charged.

**Payment terms.** Payment terms are contractual and are changed only with the corporate desk's agreement; the administrator may not change them at the service desk.

**Administrator details.** Changing the administrator's address or telephone number is free and takes effect immediately.

**What an amendment never touches.** An amendment never alters the contract term, the negotiated rates or the early exit charge, all of which follow the agreement rather than the account record.

**When a billing change bites.** Where an amendment changes what is billed, the change takes effect from the start of the next billing period and never retrospectively.

## Reach of an amendment, item by item

| Particular | Reachable by amendment | Condition or limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contracted seat count | Yes | Only within the tier's own seat range; outside it the matter is a tier change |
| Invoicing frequency | Yes | Only at a period boundary; no refund of an annual subscription already charged |
| Payment terms | Yes | Only with the corporate desk's agreement, and not at the service desk |
| Administrator's address or telephone number | Yes | Free of charge, effective immediately |
| Contract term | No | Follows the agreement, not the account record |
| Negotiated rates | No | Follows the agreement, not the account record |
| Early exit charge | No | Follows the agreement, not the account record |

## Limits worth noting

- A seat count that would fall below the tier's minimum or above its ceiling is not an amendment at all; it is a change of tier.
- A company moving from annual to monthly invoicing at a period boundary keeps no claim on the annual subscription already charged.
- A change that alters what is billed reaches the next billing period, so the period in which the amendment was made is billed as it already stood.
